title: Largest of Three
problem: Given three integers on a single line of input, separated by spaces, print the largest of the three.
starter_code:
# Read three integers from a single line of input, separated by spaces.
# Print the largest one.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Think about comparing the three numbers two at a time, or using a built-in that finds the biggest of several values.
hints.2: Python's max() function can take three arguments directly: max(a, b, c).
hints.3: a, b, c = map(int, input().split()); print(max(a, b, c))

failure_explanation: Watch out for ties (e.g. 100 100 99 should still print 100) and negative numbers (e.g. -5 -1 -9 should print -1, the one closest to zero) - a chain of if/elif that assumes the first number read is the largest will get these wrong.
